description:
## Reproducer
Discovered while implementing test-only provider integration issue zaq-o9d.4.
New test: test/zaq/channels/integration/providers/telegram_test.exs, "chat-local message ids remain independent across direct and shared chats".
In one saved Telegram connector/runtime, emit native private-chat message_id 42 in chat 123 and wait for the actual agent reply/Engine confirmation. Then emit native supergroup message_id 42 in chat -100123 with "@zaq Shared input" and a correct mention entity under default reply policy.

## Expected / actual
Expected: the second chat has an independent canonical transcript/input/execution and receives its own reply, since Telegram message IDs are chat-local.
Actual: the first direct exchange succeeds; the second update is acknowledged but discarded before creating its scoped shared transcript. Distinct-ID direct/shared scenarios pass with the same driver/fixtures. No internal routing/history/agent module is mocked.

## Source-backed diagnosis
deps/jido_chat/lib/jido/chat/handler_dispatch.ex process_message/6 checks duplicate?/2 before handler routing. dedupe_key/2 returns {adapter_name, to_string(external_message_id)} and omits the native room/chat coordinate. The single Chat state is owned per ZAQ connector, so unrelated Telegram chats collide before Engine's source-scope protections run.
Fix ownership is the shared Jido.Chat adapter/event dedupe contract; preserve existing replay behavior while respecting provider-local message namespaces.

## Scope and handling
Recorded as a blocker only. User-authorized epic zaq-o9d permits test/** and the named Mix task/repository skill, with production/application/dependency changes explicitly prohibited.
Do not patch deps, update mix.lock, prefix native fake Telegram IDs to mask the collision, skip/unregister the driver, or weaken the new test. Any production/dependency fix requires separate explicit user authorization.
Read AGENTS.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/services/channels.md, docs/services/engine.md (source-scope identity), and docs/agent-tools.md. Existing-test behavior changes require their own approval.
Required regression validation for an authorized correction: identical ID replay in one chat still dedupes; same IDs in different Telegram chats/configs remain distinct; all registered adapter regressions pass.

## Validation evidence
The Telegram provider file currently reports 5 tests, 2 failures: this chat-local-ID reproducer and the separately tracked mention_required bug. Direct/shared default flows and native API error tests pass. This failure is immediate after synchronous webhook processing, not a timing-based negative assertion.
Action reuse: not applicable to new executable operations; this ticket records a diagnosis/reproducer.

comments.text: Final validation snapshot: canonical mix q passes. Combined current integration + existing Mattermost and Telegram delivery/history regressions run 75 tests + 2 properties, with exactly the two new Telegram reproducer failures (zaq-kxd and zaq-imv). Existing tests pass. This bug blocks zaq-o9d.4. No application or dependency files were changed; a fix requires separate explicit user authorization.

title: [zaq-imv] Telegram chat-local message IDs collide in connector-wide Jido.Chat dedupe
